prompt:
A student is instructed to determine the diameter of a uniform resistance wire of length approximately 1.0 m using a micrometer screw gauge.
(a) Describe how the student should check the micrometer for a zero error before taking any measurements on the wire, and explain how a recorded zero error must be applied to subsequent measurements. [2]
(b) Describe the measurement procedure the student should follow to obtain a reliable and representative value for the diameter of the wire, explaining how both systematic errors and random errors are minimized. [3]
(c) When closed, the micrometer reads -0.03 mm. The student measures the diameter at three different locations and orientations along the wire, obtaining raw readings of 0.41 mm, 0.43 mm, and 0.42 mm. Determine the corrected mean diameter of the wire. [1]

parts.description: Check and apply zero error on micrometer
Procedure to minimize systematic and random errors

part_enrichment.guidance: Explain how to close the jaws using the ratchet until it clicks, note the reading with sign, and state that it is subtracted from raw readings.
Describe taking readings at several positions along the wire and at right angles (perpendicular orientations), applying zero correction, and averaging.
Subtract -0.03 mm from each raw reading (or from raw mean) to find corrected mean.

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (a): Close the jaws gently using the ratchet mechanism until it clicks, with nothing between the anvil and spindle.
Part (a): Record the reading on the sleeve and thimble including its sign (+ or -), and subtract this signed value from every subsequent measurement.
Part (b): Take measurements at several different positions along the length of the wire (to detect non-uniformity).
Part (b): At each position, take a second measurement at right angles / perpendicular orientation (to check for non-circular cross-section).
Part (b): Correct each reading for the systematic zero error and calculate the mean of the corrected readings to reduce random error.
Part (c): Corrected readings = 0.44 mm, 0.46 mm, 0.45 mm. Corrected mean = (0.44 + 0.46 + 0.45) / 3 = 0.45 mm.

hints: In part (a), always use the ratchet to avoid over-tightening.
In part (b), explain why taking readings at different positions and orientations is necessary for a thin wire.
In part (c), subtracting -0.03 mm adds 0.03 mm to each reading.
solution: (a) Close jaws using the ratchet until it clicks; record any non-zero reading with sign and subtract from all readings. (b) Measure at multiple positions along the wire and at mutually perpendicular orientations at each position; correct for zero error and calculate the mean. (c) Corrected readings: 0.41 - (-0.03) = 0.44 mm, 0.43 - (-0.03) = 0.46 mm, 0.42 - (-0.03) = 0.45 mm. Corrected mean = 0.45 mm.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) To check zero error: close the spindle onto the anvil using the ratchet. Read the scale. If it does not read 0.00 mm, note the sign (+ if above zero line, - if below). Corrected reading = Raw reading - (Zero error).

(b) Procedure: Measure at several points along the wire to check for uniform thickness. At each point, rotate the wire by 90 degrees to check for an oval cross-section. Correct all readings for the zero error (eliminating systematic offset) and take the mean of the corrected values (reducing random errors).
(c) Zero error is -0.03 mm. Raw readings: 0.41, 0.43, 0.42 mm.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored comprehensive 6-mark practical investigation plan for measuring wire diameter with error analysis.
